articleTitle: Introducing a novel dataset for product matching: A new challenge for matching systems
publicationTitle: 2023 5th International Communication Engineering and Cloud Computing Conference (CECCC)
abstract: Finding and matching the same product on different online shops is an essential task in many e-commerce applications such as market analysis. Most often, due to a lack of a global product identifier, this task is non-trivial. This paper describes a novel dataset for product matching that can be used to train and evaluate machine learning models that automate this task. Existing public datasets are either too small to be used for deep learning applications, use data with a present global identifier to artificially create a dataset or are too easy for state-of-the-art models. The novelty of the Markt-Pilot dataset is, that it is substantially larger than existing datasets for product matching while also consisting of real-world data that has been retrieved by querying the search function of online shops through web scraping. The dirtiness of the data and the amount of edge cases present a greater challenge for product matching systems.

articleTitle: Research on Downhole Tubing Leakage Identification Method Based on Extreme Learning Machine
publicationTitle: 2023 5th International Communication Engineering and Cloud Computing Conference (CECCC)
abstract: After the leakage of downhole tubing in gas wells, the annular space pressure between tubing and casing will be caused, which poses a certain threat to the safe production of gas wells. In this paper, the problem of downhole tubing leakage identification in gas wells is studied experimentally. The downhole tubing leakage simulation experiment device is used to simulate the tubing leakage under various working conditions. The time and frequency domain features of acoustic signals under three working conditions of no leakage, leakage location above liquid level and below liquid level are compared and analyzed. By extracting multiple features from acoustic signals as input of the model, a downhole tubing leakage identification model based on extreme learning machine (ELM) is proposed, the accuracy rate can reach 99 %.

articleTitle: A Deep Reinforcement Learning Algorithm to Project Portfolio Selection Problem
publicationTitle: 2023 5th International Communication Engineering and Cloud Computing Conference (CECCC)
abstract: Project construction and development are an important part of the development of any large organization. The most critical issue for decision-makers is how to select the right projects from the large number of candidate projects for construction and rational arrangement, that is, project portfolio selection and scheduling problem (PPSS). PPSP is a typical NP-hard problem. As the size of the problem grows, the effectiveness and practicality of traditional exact mathematical programming methods is greatly reduced due to the high time cost. Therefore, in this paper, we design a deep reinforcement learning method to solve this problem. We validate the algorithm on several datasets and compare it with metaheuristics for combinatorial optimization problems to verify the effectiveness of our algorithm.

articleTitle: Design of Intelligent Garbage Picking and Sorting Robot in Park
publicationTitle: 2023 5th International Communication Engineering and Cloud Computing Conference (CECCC)
abstract: In recent years, the people's living standards have continued to improve, which inevitably leads to an increase in the discharge of domestic garbage. The COVID-19 is raging, which has also objectively delayed the overall advancement of garbage classification. In response to the above problems, a ROS-based mobile robot that automatically picks up and classifies garbage is designed. The slam algorithm is used to build the robot's map; the ROS-based navigation framework implements the robot’ s navigation function; the robot's hardware is designed according to functional requirements The structure includes a 2D lifting garbage bucket device, which can be used in conjunction with existing trash cans; using tensorflow framework to realize trash recognition; using AR code recognition and positioning to realize precise navigation of the robot. And in the Gazebo simulation environment, the rationality and effectiveness of various functions are verified, and the design requirements are met.

articleTitle: Interaction Effect of Knowledge Network and Collaboration Network on Breakthrough Innovation
publicationTitle: 2023 5th International Communication Engineering and Cloud Computing Conference (CECCC)
abstract: The impact of knowledge networks and collaborative networks on innovation performance has been widely studied, but there is a lack of empirical research on their impact on breakthrough innovation. The aim of this study is to fill this gap by examining the non-linear relationship between inventors' ability to cross structural holes in knowledge networks and breakthrough innovation performance, while considering the moderating effects of degree centrality and collaboration centrality in collaborative networks. This study used Python and UCINET to calculate variables and used zero inflation negative binomial model to test the impact of structural holes on breakthrough innovation. The research results indicate that there is an inverted U-shaped relationship between structural holes and breakthrough innovation, and the degree centrality and closeness centrality in collaborative networks have a positive regulatory effect. The research findings reveal how the knowledge combination and collaborative relationship of inventors promote knowledge dissemination and sharing, and provide new insights for exploring collaboration and innovation.

articleTitle: A New Model for Mortgage Loss Given Default by Leveraging Time to Recovery
publicationTitle: 2023 5th International Communication Engineering and Cloud Computing Conference (CECCC)
abstract: The research report titled “A New Model for Mortgage Loss Given Default by Leveraging Time to Recovery” delves into the intricacies of credit risk, specifically focusing on the Loss Given Default (LGD) model. Credit risk pertains to the potential financial loss a lender might face due to a borrower's inability to repay a loan. The study emphasizes the significance of three models: LGD, EAD (Exposure at Default), and PD (Probability of Default) in assessing credit risk. The LGD model, in particular, represents the portion of a loan that a lender stands to lose if a borrower defaults. An essential component of this model is the Time to Recovery (<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$T$</tex> 2R), which indicates the duration required for a lender to recover the outstanding balance after a default event. The research incorporates T2R into the LGD model, addressing data censoring issues and offering a more comprehensive understanding of loss given default. Using a dataset of defaulted mortgage loans, the study identifies key influencing features and establishes correlations between LGD and T2R. The research further introduces a linear regression model and a survival model to estimate T2R. Finally, the study predicts the LGD across the sample dataset, distinguishing between open and closed episodes, highlighting the elevated risk in the open episode phase.

articleTitle: Research on Broadband Fault Detection Method for 5G Network of Distributed Smart Grid Based on Deep Learning
publicationTitle: 2023 5th International Communication Engineering and Cloud Computing Conference (CECCC)
abstract: Recently, the rapid development of 5G trusted communication technology has greatly contributed to economic and social progress, greatly improving production efficiency. However, the rapidly developing 5G communication technology will inevitably add complexity to the maintenance of network lines and energy scheduling of smart grids. In order to better safeguard the operation and maintenance of 5G communication and energy scheduling of smart grids, reduce operation and maintenance costs, and better ensure the normal scheduling of smart grid systems, this paper conducts in-depth research on the distributed smart grid inspection system of automated unmanned aerial vehicles based on large-scale data and deep learning technology, and applies image super-resolution technology to the system. A real-time fault detection method for distributed smart grid unmanned aerial vehicles based on 5G communication sites and deep learning is proposed. Specifically, the paper mainly builds a network model based on deep convolutional neural networks and attention mechanisms. The attention mechanism can effectively assign more weights to important fault features, which is beneficial for improving the performance of the model. The experimental results show that compared with existing lightweight models, the method proposed in this paper can not only improve the evaluation indicators and accurately determine whether there are faults in 5G stations and power grid dispatch systems, but also reduce the parameters and computational costs of the model. In actual deployment, the method proposed in this article can meet real-time production needs, greatly improving the efficiency of operation and maintenance, while reducing operation and maintenance costs.

articleTitle: Urban Roundabout Traffic Flow Prediction Based on GRU with Gated Recurrent Unit Structure
publicationTitle: 2023 5th International Communication Engineering and Cloud Computing Conference (CECCC)
abstract: To alleviate the problem of traffic congestion, accurately estimate the future transportation mode of the roundabout, and deal with its existent problems of periodic characteristics of traffic flow and short-term high volatility of traffic flow of the roundabout as a unique scene, this paper aims at the problem of short-term traffic flow prediction at the roundabout, a short-term traffic prediction model based on Gated Recurrent Unit (GRU) is proposed in this paper. The GRU unit learns the timing characteristics in the data and enhances the study of significant features by introducing the attention mechanism, enabling the learning of ultra-long sequences. In this paper, statistical data of TMU stations (traffic monitoring units) disclosed by the Highways Authority of the United Kingdom were extracted and input into the model for training and testing. The experimental results based on the measured data show that: Compared with RNN and LSTM, the structure used in this paper shows higher prediction accuracy in traffic flow prediction tasks. The mean absolute error (MAE) of the model reaches 1.9609, the root mean square error (RMSE) reaches 4.7279, and the mean percentage error (MAPE) reaches 13.1429%. The GRU-based model predicts traffic flow and its results can guide signal control optimization for better engineering applications.

articleTitle: An Dual-Clustering Search Strategy for Evolutionary Multi-Objective Optimization with Complicated Pareto Sets
publicationTitle: 2023 5th International Communication Engineering and Cloud Computing Conference (CECCC)
abstract: In many real-world applications, decision makers tend to approach a good approximation to the Pareto optimal set (PS) for facilitating their decision making. This is still a challenge for most existing algorithms, particularly when solving multi-objective optimization problems with complicated PS (MOP-CPSs). To address this issue, a dual-clustering search strategy-based evolutionary algorithm has been tailored for handling MOP-CPSs. Two clustering-based operators are proposed to take full advantage of the inherent advantages of clustering techniques in mining the population data structure. Firstly, the local neighborhood relationship of the population is learned in the objective space to enhance the diversity maintenance. Then, these neighborhood relationships are used to construct a mating pool in the decision space to generate offspring, with the purpose of focusing on enhancing the exploitation ability of individuals. The proposed strategy can effectively promote the overall performance in both the decision space and objective space with population iteration. The experimental results on various MOP-CPSs demonstrate that our developed algorithm outperforms several state-of-the-art multi-objective evolutionary algorithms both competitively and effectively, and shows remark-able advantages in visualization.

articleTitle: Polymorphic Cloud Application Design Assisted by Open Source Software Classification
publicationTitle: 2023 5th International Communication Engineering and Cloud Computing Conference (CECCC)
abstract: Many applications composed of more than one component or service, thus following the micro-service architecture paradigm are being deployed on the cloud exploiting advantages offered by cloud computing infrastructures such as distributed storing and computing, processing hardware (CPU, GPU, FPGA, etc), dynamic event-driven management and the support of many execution forms (serverless, container, HPC, etc) which enable the polymorphic behavior meaning, an application component can run under many execution contexts (forms and on different hardware). Considering the fluctuating nature of the workload handled by cloud applications, the cloud platform does not possess insight into the suitable form and hardware of an application component that maximizes its performance, therefore there is a need of an analysis enabling the discovery of different forms (variants) and processing units, supported by an application component, even if not specified by the application owner to allow the transition from one form or hardware to another; otherwise called cloud polymorphic adaptation. This work presents an approach consisting of discovering additional polymorphic configurations by mining the application component source code. Furthermore, the approach enables the completion of configuration for cloud components with an accuracy of at least 90%.
